name: Elijah
overview: Elijah is a male figure identified as a descendant of Elam who had married a foreign wife, as noted in Ezra 10:26. There is no record of his tribe or additional personal notes. His unique attribute highlights a connection to Elam and a foreign marriage, which situates him within the biblical narrative as a person of mixed heritage.
namesAndTitles: The name Elijah means 'YHWH is [my] God,' revealing a theologically rich connection to the LORD. This proper name underscores the centrality of God in his identity and mission, as recorded in Ezra 10:26.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Elijah as a descendant of Elam according to Ezra 10:26. Beyond this, there are no other family relationships documented for him, aside from his marriage to a foreign wife.
scriptureSignificance: Elijah's significance in Scripture is rooted in his prophetic ministry during a period of Israel's apostasy, where he boldly confronted idolatry and called the people back to the worship of the true God. His role as a powerful prophet who performed miracles and experienced divine encounters illustrates God's ongoing engagement with His people. Elijah's legacy extends into the New Testament, where his return is anticipated before the coming of the Lord, affirming his enduring place in God's redemptive plan.
